subject: Career
title: Font Psychology on Paper
description: A 60-second lesson on Font Psychology on Paper.

hook.text: A study found people judged identical statements as more true when set in Baskerville vs. Comic Sans.

buildup.text: Fonts carry emotional weight. Serif fonts feel authoritative. Sans-serif feels modern.

discovery.text: For resumes, readability wins: Calibri, Garamond, and Helvetica test best with recruiters.

twist.text: Creative fonts might feel personal but they signal 'I don't know professional norms.'

climax.text: Your font should be invisible — it should never distract from what you've achieved.

punchline.text: The best font is one nobody notices.

quiz.question: Which font characteristic is most important for resumes?

details.summary: Font choice subtly influences how recruiters perceive your professionalism and personality. Serif fonts convey tradition and reliability, sans-serif fonts communicate modernity and cleanliness, and unusual fonts suggest creativity but risk readability concerns.
details.whyItMatters: Fonts create unconscious first impressions before a single word is read. A poorly chosen font can make an excellent candidate seem unprofessional or misaligned with the industry.
takeaways: Sans-serif fonts like Calibri or Helvetica work best for most industries
Avoid decorative or script fonts entirely on professional resumes
Font size between ten and twelve points balances readability and density

faq.question: What is the safest font choice for a resume across all industries?
faq.answer: Calibri, Arial, or Helvetica in ten to twelve point size. These fonts are universally readable, render well on screens, parse correctly in ATS systems, and project professionalism without being distracting. They work for conservative and creative industries alike.

faq.question: Can creative professionals use more distinctive fonts on their resumes?
faq.answer: Creative professionals can use slightly more distinctive fonts for headers while keeping body text in standard readable fonts. The resume should hint at creativity without sacrificing readability or ATS compatibility. Save your strongest creative expression for your portfolio.
